title: Click histochemistry for whole-mount staining of brain structures
author: Lazutkin, Shuvaev, et al.

steps.title: EdU labeling and tissue collection
steps.instruction: Inject mice with 5‑ethynyl‑2′‑deoxyuridine (EdU), wait 2 h, then euthanize and dissect the whole hippocampi for whole‑mount processing.

steps.title: Bleaching
steps.instruction: Bleach the whole hippocampi for 7 h (bleaching solution and conditions as described in the original protocol).

steps.title: Rehydration
steps.instruction: Rehydrate the bleached samples for 6 h in the appropriate rehydration buffer.

steps.title: Permeabilization
steps.instruction: Permeabilize the rehydrated hippocampi for 3 h to allow reagent penetration.

steps.title: Click staining
steps.instruction: Incubate the permeabilized tissue with Alexa Fluor 555 Azide (Invitrogen, catalog A‑20012) for 2 h to perform the Cu(I)‑catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition (click) reaction that labels incorporated EdU.

steps.title: Rinsing
steps.instruction: Rinse the stained hippocampi for about 24 h (multiple washes as in the original protocol) to remove unbound azide.

steps.title: Optical clearing
steps.instruction: Clear the rinsed samples for an additional 2 days using the clarified solution described in the method (details not specified in the excerpt).

steps.title: Mounting for imaging
steps.instruction: Place 2 to 6 hippocampal pieces on a glass slide inside a square silicone frame, fill the frame with the clarifying solution, cover with a coverslip while avoiding air bubbles, outline the coverslip borders with a hydrophobic marker, and add distilled water inside the outlined borders.

steps.title: Confocal imaging
steps.instruction: Image the mounted specimens on an Olympus FluoView 1000 upright laser‑scanning confocal microscope using a water‑immersion objective UM Plan FL N 20x/0.50 W. Acquire Z‑stacks through the full depth (up to 1.5 mm) with a step size of 5 μm, collect 25–35 fields of view, and stitch them into a 3‑D reconstruction using Imaris 6.0 (Bitplane).

steps.title: Alternative light‑sheet imaging
steps.instruction: Optionally image the cleared whole‑mount hippocampi using light‑sheet microscopy as described in reference [6].

description: A method described here allows staining whole brain structures using the Cu (I) -catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloaddition reaction (so-called click-reaction) between the terminal ethynyl group incorporated into DNA upon 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) injection and fluorescently labeled azide. This method can be used in neurogenesis studies, i.e. for birthdating of dividing early progenitors and further tracking of proliferation, survival, migration, differentiation, and fate of their progeny. This whole-mount click method is based on the original protocol for staining tissue sections developed by Salic and Mitchison [1]. The following procedures were developed and optimized for whole hippocampus preparation staining and imaging. To validate the method, we visualized dividing cells in the whole hippocampi of 2-week-, 2-month- and 12-month-old nestin-CFPnuc mice [7]. Dividing cells were labeled with EdU 2 h before euthanasia. Whole-mount click histochemistry was performed using Alexa Fluor 555 Azide (Invitrogen, A-20012). Overall, the protocol included bleaching (7 h), rehydration (6 h), permeabilization (3 h), staining (2 h), and rinsing (about 24 h), with the total duration of 4 days excluding the time required for sample preparation. The optical clearing procedures took additional 2 days. Examples of mouse whole-mount hippocampi stained using click histochemistry are presented in Fig. 1. Our whole-mount click histochemistry method achieved high staining specificity, high signal intensity, and low background levels both in young and adult hippocampi. Sparse dividing cells were found in all layers of hippocampus, while high labeled cell density was evident in the dentate gyrus, a brain area where neurogenesis occurs throughout life in rodents.
